The public synthetic App Attest object comes from [Apple's validation guide](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/attestation-object-validation-guide), retrieved 2026-10-16, and describes the fictitious `1234567890.com.example.myapp` app.

Full positive verification uses its published historical context: 2026-04-21 18:13:13 UTC, OS executable category 1, bundle version `1` and raw `example_server_challenge` client-hash bytes. The object appends documented authenticator extensions without setting the extensions bit. These are explicit test inputs, never production control configuration: production uses the current time, the publisher's fixed App ID, SHA256 of the signed challenge and TestFlight/App Store categories 2 or 4. Both certificate paths still use the unmodified pinned Apple roots, and CMS signature, receipt app/key/hash and freshness are verified.

The fixture is rejected outside its historical context, for a wrong app, environment or category, a stale receipt or a tampered signature. It does not authenticate Collie or replace genuine-device acceptance.

`assertions.json` holds fixed synthetic regression proofs for `TESTTEAM01.dev.rbstp.collie`, signed with Node's `crypto.sign('sha256', nonce, key)` and a disposable P-256 key, since discarded. Positive proofs sign `SHA256(authenticatorData || SHA256(challenge))`, following [Apple's assertion verification steps](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/validating-apps-that-connect-to-your-server); negative proofs sign the unhashed concatenation or carry unexpected credential bytes. Ordinary and retained-AT-flag assertions are both covered.
